clue.text: Money is better — land contracts

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it

indicators.note: a word that contracts gets shorter, so the country loses its final letter

parts.note: Italy is a land, a country

explanation.surface: A property tip: land is the best money-maker, as long as the contracts are signed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracts' looks like a noun about land deals, but it is a verb telling you to shorten ITALY to ITAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital is wealth or funds available for investment, a standard synonym for cash.

clue.text: Dog with stick up on deserted Exmoor

parts.note: to cock ears or a tail is to make them stick up

indicators.note: deserted means the place is emptied, keeping only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A dog with its tail in the air on lonely Exmoor.
explanation.walkthrough: Exmoor is moorland in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocker spaniel is a breed of dog.

clue.text: Kitty eating a bishop's bird

indicators.note: eating means the pot swallows the next letters

parts.note: a kitty is a pot of shared money
RR stands for Right Reverend, a bishop's title

explanation.surface: A cat eating a bishop's pet bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitty' is not a cat but a fund of money, a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A parrot is a brightly coloured bird known for mimicking speech.

clue.text: Backing up computer work, restoring deleted spreadsheet, initially for owners' documents

indicators.note: in a down entry backing up means the letters run upwards, in reverse

parts.note: IT is information technology, computer work

indicators.note: restoring means the letters of the clue word are reassembled
initially means only the opening letter of the spreadsheet is used

explanation.surface: An IT task: making backups and recovering a deleted spreadsheet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restoring' rearranges DELETED into TLEDEED; 'Backing up' turns IT into TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Title deeds are legal papers proving who owns a property.

clue.text: Can run inside to get American grub

indicators.note: inside says the run letter sits within the toilet word

parts.note: can is slang for a toilet, as is lav
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Can you nip in and fetch some American food?
explanation.walkthrough: 'grub' sounds like food but is the insect sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub is an insect larva, the worm-like young stage of a beetle.

clue.text: Deviate from act in motion

parts.note: a turn is a performer's act on a variety bill
runners who are off have started moving

explanation.surface: A director's note about straying from the planned action in a scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave a road for a side road is to depart or deviate from the main route.

clue.text: Doctor protects drug, making injection for certain people only

indicators.note: making injection says the drug letter is injected into the rest
to doctor something is to tamper with it, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is ecstasy, a drug

explanation.surface: A doctor guards a confidential drug for an injection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' rearranges PROTECTS into TOPSCRET, and E goes into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Classified information is meant to be seen by a few named people, and no one else.

clue.text: Smell bottom of toddler — it's alarming!

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its final letter

parts.note: eek is the cry of alarm

explanation.surface: A parent's horror at a whiff from a toddler's nappy.
explanation.definitionFit: To reek is to give off a strong, unpleasant smell.

clue.text: Went round green filling in two holes in order

indicators.note: filling in means the green word fills the gap between the two holes

parts.note: O looks like a hole, so two holes give two Os
vert is green in heraldry
OK means all in order

explanation.surface: A golfer going round the green, sinking two holes in a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' and 'holes' suggest golf; they are heraldry and letter shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: To go round a slower vehicle is to pass, i.e. overtake, it.

clue.text: Rich celebrity who believes in destiny

parts.note: rich food is fat or fatty
an A-list celebrity is a top star

explanation.surface: A wealthy star who trusts in fate.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatalist holds that events are fixed in advance and cannot be changed.

clue.text: Carpet Power's removed mark

indicators.note: removed says that letter is taken out of the floor covering's name

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: Someone named Power has had a carpet taken away, leaving a stain.
explanation.definitionFit: A caret is the small proofreading symbol marking where text should be inserted.

clue.text: Act on stage

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
to stage a show is to present it

explanation.surface: A simple instruction to perform on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase; split it so 'Act' is the definition and 'on stage' the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To act for someone, as an agent or lawyer does, is to speak on their behalf.

clue.text: Naughty individual goes in after energy is discharged

indicators.note: after says the rest of the wordplay follows the energy letter

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: goes in says the word for a single person is put inside the film rating

parts.note: an X-rated film is a naughty, adults-only one
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: A naughty person sneaks into a room once the power has gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cleared of blame has been released from the charge, i.e. discharged of guilt.

clue.text: Worried about novice and others

indicators.note: about means the word for worried is turned round

parts.note: ate, as in 'what's eating you?', means worried
L is the learner plate on a novice driver's car

explanation.surface: Someone fretting about a beginner, and about everyone else too.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin abbreviation is used in lists and citations to mean 'and the rest'.

clue.text: Gets up on time, not good getting rest

parts.note: stands means gets up
ill means bad, not good

explanation.surface: Someone stands up on schedule despite feeling poorly, needing rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete halt in motion is a state of rest.

clue.text: Assertions from Aldi: 'Tesco ran badly'

indicators.note: badly says these supermarket names are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A rival grocer's claim that Tesco ran its business poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: Aldi and Tesco are British supermarket chains.
explanation.definitionFit: Declarations are formal statements, which is to say assertions of fact.

clue.text: American, however, is extremely thick

definitions.meaning: used in the US as a word meaning at least, anyway
read as two words: wise to the smallest degree, i.e. very stupid

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer in two: the lowest amount of wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiefly in American English the word is an informal way of saying anyway or at any rate.

clue.text: They reckon a bad copper enters section

indicators.note: enters says the copper symbol goes into the word for bad

parts.note: base means morally low, bad
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A corrupt police officer joins a department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' is a police officer on the surface, the metal in the parse.
explanation.definitionFit: Counting frames with beads are used for reckoning, i.e. doing calculations.

clue.text: Place for knocking shop at the back: make love with rest when light goes on

indicators.note: goes on says the shop letter is added at the end

parts.note: to do is to make, as in 'do lunch'
love is zero in tennis, O

indicators.note: light here means alight or set off, so the letters of rest move about
at the back means only the final letter of shop is used

explanation.surface: A saucy scene in a brothel: love-making, then sleep once the light is on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking shop' is British slang for a brothel, but the definition is just 'Place for knocking'. 'when light' rearranges REST into STE.
explanation.definitionFit: You stand on the step outside a front door when you knock on it.

clue.text: See 25
Fruity thing with desire to get laid regularly outside

indicators.note: outside says those picked letters go round the desire word
regularly means every other letter of laid is taken

parts.note: an itch is a restless desire

explanation.surface: A cheeky line about someone with an urge to sleep around.
explanation.definitionFit: The lychee, also spelt this way, is a sweet Chinese fruit.

clue.text: Upset sergeant major goes off and attacks

indicators.note: in a down entry upset means turned upside down, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: SM is the military abbreviation for sergeant major
food that goes off rots

explanation.surface: An angry sergeant major loses his temper and goes on the offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops who storm a position make a violent assault on it.

clue.text: Vehicle needing day to book

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A hire car is needed for a day, so someone must book it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book' is a verb: a referee cards (books) a player by showing a yellow card.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, booking a player for a foul means showing him a yellow card.

clue.text: Cook steak dinner primarily? Win, having lost weight with it?

definitions.text: Cook steak dinner primarily? Win, having lost weight with it?

indicators.note: cook means the pieces are worked into a new order, as ingredients are
primarily picks out just the opening letter of the meal word
having lost says a letter is dropped from the word win

explanation.surface: Is cooking mostly steak for dinner the way to win at slimming?
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost' takes W from WIN, leaving IN; STEAK, D, IN and IT are shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes a high-protein, low-carbohydrate slimming regime built on meat like steak.

clue.text: Standard paper to deliver

parts.note: the i is a British newspaper
to deal cards or a blow is to deliver it

explanation.surface: A routine paper round delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a standard of perfection to aim for.

clue.text: Further part for choral society

indicators.note: part says the letters form a piece of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Looking for an extra singing part for the choir.
explanation.definitionFit: Also means in addition, i.e. furthermore.

clue.text: TV work to state Clare Balding is racing

indicators.note: racing words are moving fast and furiously, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A TV job to tell viewers Clare Balding is presenting the horse racing.
explanation.walkthrough: Clare Balding is a British sports presenter famous for horse-racing coverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Transmitting television programmes via orbiting craft is a kind of TV work.

clue.text: Suffer through short treatment

parts.note: in can mean by way of or through, as in 'in the post'

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a cure is a course of medical treatment

explanation.surface: Someone suffering because their medical treatment was cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a loss or penalty is to bring it on oneself and so suffer it.

clue.text: Matter for reflection: sit and think

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror is reversed, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: pus is the matter in an infected wound
to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: A meditation instruction: here is something to reflect on, so sit and think.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppose is to assume or believe, a straightforward synonym for think.

clue.text: I'm laughing with Tales For Suckers

parts.note: LOL, text slang for laughing out loud
tales can be fibs or lies

explanation.surface: Laughing at a book of stories for gullible people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suckers' suggests dupes, but here it means things you suck.
explanation.definitionFit: Lollipops are sweets on sticks, things you suck, so they are suckers.
